annotations.text:
Pawgress MVP wireframes — Sprint 04

Low fidelity on purpose: greyscale, no brand, no type personality. Colour, mascot and icon set are Sprint 05; components are Sprint 06.

All frames are 360px wide — the cheapest phone a student owns. Top row: onboard, organise, upload, review. Bottom row: practise, assess, ask.
No floating action button. A full-width labelled button is bigger, clearer and reachable one-handed. Chrome budget: 48px header + 56px tabs + 56px action — nothing else gets to be sticky.
Page citations on every section are the product, not decoration. A reviewer that cannot cite its source is treated as a failed generation, not shown as a reviewer.
Focus mode: no tabs, no sidebar, one exit. Verdict buttons stay disabled until the card is flipped, so a student cannot mark a card they never read.
The quota cost is shown BEFORE the tap, and answers save on every tap so a phone reload never loses an attempt. Both are cheap to build now and impossible to retrofit politely.
The score is not the point — the next action is. Wrong answers open by default, correct ones collapse, and 'ask why I got this wrong' is the highest-value link in the app.
Scope is pinned to the top so 'my materials' always means something specific. A general-knowledge answer is an explicit opt-in, never silently mixed in.
